messages:
Sam G: heads-up — saw a weird divergence after the int8 bring-up for ranker-v3 on the longform bench. dev ndcg +0.9% but mrr on short queries dropped ~2.8%. putting quick repro below.
Mira K: ouch. can you paste the exact eval command + which dataset slices this touched?
Sam G: sure — ran the usual eval harness against `candidate-holdout-v2` with the new ptq recipe. command: 
```
./eval_harness.sh --model=ranker-v3-int8 --candidates=candidate-holdout-v2 --slices=short_queries,long_docs --metrics=ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed=42
```
Raw snippet: `ndcg@10: +0.009 (p=0.03)`, `mrr@10 (short_queries): -0.028 (p=0.001)`. full output attached to the run but that's the headline.
Jonathan: important Qs — is this a rerank vs rescoring change? candidate ordering stable? also was the tokenizer or doc concat logic touched in the build that went into int8?
Sam G: rerank (scoring only), candidate ordering unchanged. tokenizer code unchanged in tree AFAICT. the only diffs in the optimized build were: PTQ per-channel symmetric quant params + changes to prefix padding to optimize batch shapes.
Eva L: padding change could alter tokenization/truncation alignment for short queries vs long documents. short queries may get more aggressive truncation on the candidate text if padding/layout changed. worth checking. :thinking:
Mira K: also check embed scale/normalization — sometimes int8 rescales float logits differently and that affects top-1 lots. can you run slice-level calibration?
Sam G: running slice breakdown now. quick numbers:
- overall ndcg@10: +0.9%
- mrr@10 (short_queries): -2.8% (n=4.2k queries)
- mrr@10 (long_docs): +0.4% (n=1.1k)
- top1 accuracy (short): -3.5%
Jonathan: n=4.2k is not tiny. p=0.001 suggests signal. can you repro deterministically with fixed batching params (force batch_size=1) to rule out batching reorder?
Sam G: good call. switching to single-thread single-batch run now — will post diff.
eval-bot: CI: started reproduce job 4765432100-1 (single-batch). ETA ~12m.
Mira K: also try running the float32 baseline with the same padding/layout that the int8 build uses — if layout alone causes the drop, we'll see it in float too.
Sam G: copied. plan: (1) run float32 with new padding/layout; (2) run int8 with old padding/layout; (3) run int8 single-batch; (4) ablation: per-channel vs per-tensor quant. will update results here.
Eva L: if it persists after layout/ batching ablations, next step is to inspect top-100 candidate score distributions for short queries and compare z-score shifts. small global bias can wreck mrr without harming ndcg much.
Jonathan: agree. also check tokenization boundaries/whether stopwords get dropped on concatenation boundary after padding change — can create off-by-one context differences.
Sam G: update (12m): single-batch int8 run finished. mrr(short) still down ~2.7%. float32 with new padding/layout shows mrr(short) stable (no drop). int8 with old padding/layout not run yet.
Mira K: that points to quantization math rather than layout. run int8 per-tensor variant and dump per-layer scale params.
Sam G: kicked per-tensor job. also dumping top-10 candidate scores for 30 failed short queries for manual inspection. attaching sample diff: 
```
query_id: q12345
float_scores: [2.34, 1.98, 1.20, ...]
int8_scores:  [2.31, 1.92, 1.05, ...]  # third candidate drops relatively more
```
Eva L: looks like head bias on mid-ranked candidates. PTQ often compresses logits tail. try small calibration shift (add epsilon per-layer) and eval a cheap correction to see if MRR recovers.
Jonathan: also check if LN/fused ops got slightly reordered in the optimized kernels — that can change numeric order. compare op graph hashes between float and int8 builds.
Sam G: good notes. per-tensor int8 run completed: result = mrr(short) -2.4% (still down but slightly better). per-channel was -2.7. so per-tensor slightly helps but not fixed.
Mira K: incremental improvement suggests quant granularity matters. try fine-tuning with 1-2 steps on a small calibration set (post-quant fnl) — tiny FT often recovers head order.
Sam G: launching 2-step quant-finetune on 10k short-queries. also opening a small canary to prod for dedicated slice if we get +0.5% mrr back.
Eva L: agree on canary. doc of follow-ups: 1) run top-100 z-score shift for short queries (Sam), 2) try tiny FT (Sam), 3) graph/ op hash diff (Jonathan), 4) try per-tensor/ asymmetric configs (Mira). will sync in tomorrow's rerank stand. :thumbsup:
